intended_object: The degree-zero cocycles Z⁰(Hom_𝒞(X,Y)) = {f ∈ Hom⁰(X,Y) : m₁ f = 0} of the morphism complex in an A∞-category. These are the representatives of morphisms in the homotopy category H⁰(𝒞) (docstring, module doc, Keller §7.1).
explanation:
The definition is the intersection of two submodules of the graded Hom module Hom(X,Y): the degree-0 piece of its grading, and the kernel of `homDifferential X Y`. `homDifferential X Y` is m₁ restricted to that Hom component: it includes the morphism into the total morphism algebra, applies the differential m₁ there, and projects back to the Hom component. So the definition gives exactly the closed degree-zero morphisms {f ∈ Hom⁰(X,Y) : m₁ f = 0}, which matches the docstring and Keller's description of the morphisms representing H⁰(𝒞).

The setting is already general: any commutative ring R and any A∞-category structure on a graded linear quiver. Mathlib has no notion of A∞-category, so there is no more general counterpart to point to.
